Faculty review: Mhr3 (Dr. Mohammad Harisur Rahman) 
Course: Ant101
Also recommended for: Pol101/Soc101/Tnm201
Had the experience of doing two courses (Ant101,Tnm201) under his supervision. He is quite a charm and chill person. His teaching technique is very elaborative, because of exampling each and every source of data. Tricks: To pull out the best, try to score as much as possible in the mid and final. He takes two quizzes (from which best one is count), and an assignment (group project).

) 
Peace!

ztz.review:
Faculty Review - ZTZ (Zarin Tasnim Ma’am)
I took TNM201 under ZTZ ma’am last semester, and honestly, she’s one of the friendliest and most easygoing faculties I’ve come across. At first, I was hesitant about taking her section because of a few negative reviews I’d seen. Unfortunately, there are only 2–3 reviews about her across all the groups, and most of them are negative. Everyone’s experience is different, but I feel like ma’am deserves a genuine review so more students can consider taking her section.
She’s super sweet, funny, friendly, and incredibly accommodating. She teaches really well and makes the classes lively and fun. Throughout the semester, she’s been very considerate and has given almost everyone a chance to make up for their shortcomings or mistakes. There’s absolutely no pressure in her class. Exams are straightforward, and she marks quite leniently. Plus, she grades fairly and even curves the grades for top performers.
To conclude, don’t hesitate to take her section! She’s genuinely amazing, and you’ll learn a lot while having a fun and stress-free experience. See less
Indeed! I did TNM201 under her too! Such a sweetheart!

I totally agree. She’s the best!

kfm.review:
If you are considering taking TNM201 for open elective, this post is for you:
Faculty Review
Faculty Initial: KFM 
K M M Ashfaq Ul Mushfiq 
Course: TNM201
TNM201 is a fun and interesting course where you will learn basic media theories, how film and theater work, how a news channel operates, and much more.
Mushfiq sir is very dedicated to his work and is the best at it. He knows how to engage the classroom and prevent students from feeling bored. You don't have to memorize everything if you attend classes regularly; he will explain each topic like a storyteller. I am sure you will enjoy his classes.
**Pros** 
- Teaches very well. Friendly and helpful
- Will give suggestions before exams on how to score well
- Movie suggestions will help in the Mid and Final exams 
- Will show all your marks
- Questions will come from his lectures
Although it was his first semester, he was well-prepared before every lecture. He took two quizzes and averaged the marks, and there was one midterm, one report, and one presentation, and one viva (for some reason, he couldn't take our viva).
For our study tour, we went to the Jamuna TV Channels office, which was interesting and fun. If you follow his instructions, you will not need any curving. He will give you your deserved grades.
You might not have found any reviews as it was his first semester, and he was supervising only one section of TNM201 course along with two Media courses this semester. I would highly recommend TNM201 as a free elective course for BBA students. See less
